request: Prepare a 45-minute lesson comparing an object-level condition proportion with an equal-batch mean. Students must show why the two happen to agree here and why that coincidence is not a general pooling rule.
objective: Explain equal results under unequal group sizes without confusing equal rates with equal weights.

sources.text: Fictional archive condition survey: batch Amber contained eight boxes, and two met the dry-storage checklist. Batch Slate contained twenty-eight boxes, and seven met the same checklist. Both batches were inspected on Monday using identical criteria.
Every box has a unique inventory ID and belongs to exactly one batch. No box was counted in both. Packing materials and prior storage histories were not recorded.
The archivist requests the proportion among all inspected boxes, while an assistant proposes the simple average of the two batch rates. No other archive boxes were inspected in this survey.
